Nothing here changes a pick, a probability or a model by itself: the owner decides.

glossary.modelProbability: Probability produced by a statistical model from its feature snapshot. It is not a confidence level and it is not derived from prices.
glossary.marketProbability: Consensus probability across tracked bookmakers after removing the overround. It is not the raw implied probability of a single price.
glossary.impliedProbability: Raw 1 / odds of a single bookmaker price. It still contains the bookmaker margin, so it always sums above 100% across a market.
glossary.fairOdds: Price that would make a selection break even at the model probability: 1 / model probability. It is not an available price.
glossary.bestOdds: Highest price currently captured for the selection across tracked bookmakers.
glossary.edge: Model probability minus market probability, in percentage points. Requires both a model probability and an available price to exist.
glossary.ev: Expected value: model probability multiplied by the available price, minus one. It is an arithmetic property of the inputs, not a profitability claim.
glossary.brier: Multi-class Brier score: squared error between the predicted probabilities and the outcome, summed over the outcomes and averaged over matches. Lower is better; 1/3 on each of home, draw and away scores 0.667.
glossary.logLoss: Negative log likelihood of the observed outcomes under the predicted distribution. Punishes confident mistakes harshly. Lower is better.
glossary.calibration: Agreement between predicted probability and observed frequency. A perfectly calibrated model lies on the diagonal of the reliability curve.
glossary.calibrationError: Expected calibration error (ECE): the gap between predicted probability and observed frequency in ten equal-width probability bins, weighted by how many predictions fall in each bin (every outcome of every match counts).
glossary.vsMarket: Model log loss minus the de-vigged market's log loss on the fixtures both priced, with a 95% paired-bootstrap interval. Negative means the model scored better. 'Better' is claimed only when the whole interval is below zero.
glossary.hypotheticalBetting: A backtest simulation: flat one-unit stakes at the historical source's closing price, by a rule fixed before the test season. It is not a record of bets and not a forecast of returns.
glossary.historicalClosing: Closing and pre-closing prices as published by Football-Data.co.uk. They are the source's labels, not prices this platform captured, and they carry no exact timestamp.
glossary.nearClose: Price captured close to kickoff (T-12m). It is not validated as an official closing price and must not be reported as closing line value.
glossary.pickLineValue: Difference between the price recorded on a pick and a later reference price. Requires validated near-close capture before it can be reported.
glossary.overround: Sum of raw implied probabilities across a market. Values above 1 represent the bookmaker margin.
glossary.reliability: Qualitative assessment of how much weight the sample, coverage and model status justify. It is not a probability.
glossary.freshness: Age of the most recent successful capture relative to the freshness thresholds.
glossary.sampleSize: Number of scored observations behind a metric. Small samples cannot separate skill from noise.
glossary.drawdown: Largest peak-to-trough decline of a cumulative series.
glossary.yieldMetric: Profit divided by total amount staked. Requires settled, published picks.
glossary.roi: Return on investment across settled picks. Not computable without validated results.
